projects.title: ADHD Project Manager
projects.hook: A scheduled scan that catches everything I leave midway across AI chats and lands it on one prioritized board. Built for my ADHD; built so anyone can repurpose it.

body.problem: AI chats are where work goes to die midway — brilliant threads abandoned, commitments unconfirmed, and no single place to see what's actually open.
body.approach: A scheduled scan reads every thread, finds open loops, and lands them on one prioritized board: sense → draft → queue → review.
body.hers: Designed from my own failure modes — ADHD as a design constraint, never an apology. Produced is not shipped.
body.result: One board, every open loop, ranked. The scan runs daily; I clear it in one sitting.
body.lesson: The job isn't organizing tasks. It's noticing them.

projects.title: Claude Skills
projects.hook: Two skills for finding what I already figured out. One moves knowledge between Claude projects. The other helps when I'm in the right project and can't name what I want.
projects.metric: 2 skills · open source · free to install
projects.visualAlt: Two Claude skills: cross-project-extraction and retrieval-coach
projects.diagramAlt: One trip with three stops, and the retrieval coach flow

body.problem: I work across several Claude projects. What I figure out in one stays locked there, and even in the right project I often can't find the words to search for it.
body.approach: Treat the search as a planned trip: pack a brief at home, search at the destination, unpack back home. A copy-paste block carries the context, because Claude has no memory across projects. A second skill coaches the query before any search runs.
body.hers: Both started as workarounds I got tired of repeating. I think in patterns first and the words come later, so the coach shows why a keyword worked. Querying is a muscle I want to train.
body.result: Two skills, published with the problem behind each, setup notes and limits. Anyone can install them in a few minutes.
body.lesson: Project isolation is a constraint to design around. A good handoff block does more than shared memory would.

prototyping: More tools are in the workshop — each one earns its card here when it has a live demo and a written playbook.
